A Cut Above The Rest
Mar 2014 • Couples
We ate here several times during our stay in Nha Trang and found it to be one of the best restaurants, at which we ate, throughout our trip.

There is a fantastic choice of dishes, many of which we hadn't seen anywhere else. Having been lucky enough to be invited for dinner at the home of a local Vietnamese, this restaurant came the closest to replicating home cooked Vietnamese food of any that we experienced throughout Vietnam.

Prices were very reasonable, staff were always friendly and helpful and whilst the surroundings are simple, the atmosphere was always warm and enjoyable. The close setting encourages friendly conversation with other diners, if one desires this.

Located in a major tourist area, at the Southern End of town, it's a block away from the main Vietnamese Airlines office, so should be easy enough to find.

We found the quality of restaurants to be extremely variable in Nha Trang but this was definitely a cut above the rest and is worth making an effort to seek out.

Review Redux
Mar 2013 • Couples
Com Ngon Lanh - Review 03-05-13

I reviewed this restaurant a little over 14 months ago. Sadly, the same experience was not had this evening, and I have to agree with most of the recent ‘average’ reviews and czhunty’s review of March 2012, “I was expecting local priced gem as it used to be..”. I also concur with jeera27’s review of 2-23-12, which was the reason we returned last night.

We arrived at the restaurant just before 7 pm. We waited for a server to seat us, even though there was only one table available on the first floor, where we were placed next to a couple guys that were smoking. Normally, I don’t mind sitting near smokers if the area is open air or there are some fans blowing. We had to move the table a bit away from them.

There was only one server, shuttling plates of food up and down the restaurant's two floors. In addition, she was taking orders, handling dinner bills and returning change. When we ate here in December of 2011, there were no less than two or three wait staff. We were handed a batch of menus (five I think) to peruse while I waited for a beverage. Like the last time, the menu is the most extensive one I’ve seen in Asia. Is that now a problem? Do they now offer so much to choose from they cannot provide a few spectacular offerings?

We finally ended up choosing two bowls of Hu Tieu - My Tho (40,000d each), Fried ‘Chem” (chim?) fish, perhaps also known as pomfret (55,000d), and Roasted duck, Peking style (70,000d). Oh yes, we also had to pay for steamed rice (5,000d). It’s a minimal price but sort of insulting when so many other restaurants would include steamed rice with your entrée. The Saigon beer was the same price as last year (15,000d), which is sort of a surprise since our total bill was half again as much as it was last year and the server said that we only ordered one bowl of Hu Tieu, when I quite sure that we had ordered two but only received one. Was she so busy and stressed that she got the order wrong? 

My wife is from My Tho, and she said the Hu Tieu - My Tho was nothing like what they serve in the Delta region. I agreed. The server didn’t even offer to bring us out another bowl if we chose to order and pay for one, so we passed.

The fried fish, even though it was a flat fish, was overcooked or overfried. It didn’t have much body to it, and it certainly wasn’t moist. The same went for the duck. To be clear, we expected small portions for the price paid but they were not prepared as nicely as in December 2011. Had the restaurant changed hands since our last visit?

Unfortunately, the service was much less than expected and the food was not worth the price charged for the portions served. The only item that shined at dinner was the Saigon beer, still the same price and quality of a product not substantially controlled by the restaurant. The pendulum has swung - 2.5 stars.
